$comment: Run B ran with performance/compose.perf-override.yml active. The baseline artifact produced by run-baseline.sh carries no field for this, which is why it is recorded here alongside it -- the tooling was deliberately not modified before Run B, so that Run B measured the same benchmark implementation Run A did. Making the baseline schema itself carry this fact is part of the separately-tracked tooling fix.
evidence_identity: R1 Run B — capacity characterization / perf rate-limit override
disposition: VALID / PASS — capacity characterization only, NOT a production-policy result

performance_rate_limit_override.purpose_per_file_header: probe above the IP rate-limit ceiling so the run measures the application rather than the limiter
performance_rate_limit_override.note: The two SUBJECT_* values are set by the override file but are not read by this build: application.yml exposes only security.rate-limit.capacity and .refill-per-second, both keyed on client IP. Only the IP tier was actually relaxed.

relationship_to_run_a: Run B does not replace, supersede or relabel Run A. Run A is the canonical result under production rate-limit policy. Run B answers only the question Run A could not: what the application does when the infrastructure protection ceiling is not the binding constraint.
